elements.element: Fallback: mutual right for each party to assign to a successor (merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets)
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets related to this Agreement without such consent"(unchanged)

elements.element: Fallback: written notice to the other party of such successor assignment
elements.evidence: No notice obligation appears anywhere in the redlined Section 14.1; the successor carve-out operates "without such consent" and is silent on notice.

elements.element: Fallback: consent for other (non-successor) assignments not to be unreasonably withheld
elements.evidence: "without the prior written consent of the other party, which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld, conditioned or delayed"

elements.element: Preferred: Customer may assign without consent to an affiliate
elements.evidence: The only affiliate carve-out runs to the counterparty: "provided that Corio may assign this Agreement ... to any entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with Corio without such consent".

elements.element: Preferred: Customer may assign without consent to a successor in merger/acquisition/asset sale
elements.evidence: "either party shall have the right to assign this Agreement in connection with the merger or acquisition of such party or the sale of all or substantially all of its assets"

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor may not assign without Customer's consent (not unreasonably withheld)
elements.evidence: Vendor now has a consent-free affiliate route: "provided that Corio may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with Corio without such consent".

elements.element: Preferred: Vendor may never assign to a Customer competitor
elements.evidence: Competitor transfers are only consent-gated, not prohibited: "except in the case where such transaction involves a direct competitor of the other party where consent of the other party will be required".

elements.element: Preferred: no Vendor termination right on Customer's change of control
elements.evidence: No change-of-control termination right is created or preserved in Section 14.1 (condition demonstrably absent in the clause).

offending_extra_words: provided that Corio may assign this Agreement, in whole or in part, to any entity controlling, controlled by or under common control with Corio without such consent
reasons: Fallback is incomplete: the written-notice element for successor assignments is never inserted, so the clause still permits silent successor transfers by the Vendor.

The edit grants the counterparty (Corio, the Vendor) an unqualified, consent-free right to assign in whole or in part to any affiliate. That is a new one-sided exception in the Vendor's favour and directly contradicts the playbook position that Vendor may not assign without Customer consent; the reciprocal Customer affiliate right was not added.

Minimality fails: the operation expands a 12-word anchor to 49 words (ratio 4.08) and changes 74% of characters, when the fallback needed only the short insertion "which consent shall not be unreasonably withheld" (plus a notice phrase).
"in whole or in part" and "conditioned or delayed" are surplus to the fallback bargain; the partial-assignment language additionally lets the Vendor split obligations among affiliates.
The margin comment describes the carve-out as addressing "customer assignments", but the operative text confers it on Corio only — a mismatch that should be corrected before sending.
